parallel.requirements: Recognized all six requirements: four IR-builder modules plus assembly code generation and register management, with release build and tests required before completion.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used native swarm mode with five child agents: four frontend owners and one combined backend owner; the parent kept integration, testing, and per-requirement commits for itself.
parallel.implementation: Child results reported implemented frontend modules and backend files; the parent integrated them enough for a successful release build and Koopa generation on hello.c.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After all five child results returned, the parent built the project and began integrated sample testing, but the git log captured no per-requirement implementation commits beyond the initial workspace state.
parallel.verification: Release build succeeded and Koopa output for the sample looked plausible, but the subsequent RISC-V generation command failed with Error: Global value must have a name.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run closed under provider rate-limit retries after the visible RISC-V/global failure; official evaluation failed seven global, array, and nested-if related cases.

serial.requirements: Read the same six requirement files directly and round 2 resumed with frontend requirements complete and asm_code_gen plus asm_register_allocator remaining.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Maintained a single-agent serial control with no delegation; the agent owned each implementation, commit, build, and test step across two rounds.
serial.implementation: Implemented and committed frontend requirements in round 1, then committed the register allocator and wrote a complete build_assembly.rs backend in round 2.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built the release binary after backend work; the final captured git log contains the frontend commits and the register allocator commit, while the official run evaluated the resulting workspace.
serial.verification: Ran release builds and additional self-tests; custom qemu tests exposed a separate gp/linker-relaxation concern late, but the completed official evaluation passed every listed case.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial agent was interrupted by provider rate limit after diagnosing a local bare-metal/qemu issue, but the current official status reports solution_passed true.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent recognized the six required compiler areas and explicitly split them into frontend files plus a combined backend assignment.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run read the same requirements directly and resumed round 2 with four frontend requirements complete and both backend requirements remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the task scope; the difference is not requirement awareness but that serial continued the remaining backend work in one local control flow while parallel discovered an unresolved backend/global failure after joining children.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent delegated four frontend files to separate children and the two backend files to one backend child, while reserving integration, tests, and commits for itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had no child agents; it implemented frontend requirements over round 1 and then owned the backend continuation in round 2.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ownership was explicit and joined, but spread across child handoffs; serial kept implementation and correction inside one sequential workspace context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received specific file/requirement briefs and all five summaries came back to the parent before integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained its own context across commits and round 2 began from the existing patches and remaining backend requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete lost, stale, overloaded, or conflicting handoff is visible in parallel; the main contrast is serial did not need to reduce multi-child handoffs before diagnosing backend behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assembled child implementations and produced Koopa for the sample, but RISC-V generation on that same sample failed with a global-value naming error.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the backend implementation directly in round 2 after committing the register allocator and reached a buildable compiler used by the official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete task-solving gap is in the backend/global/array path: parallel left an executable RISC-V generation failure, while serial completed enough backend behavior for all official global and array cases to pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All five child results were returned to the parent; the parent then moved to integrated build and testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagent result lifecycle and instead used local commits and continuation state between rounds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no missing join, unreturned verifier, or unused completed result in parallel; serial simply avoided that lifecycle surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated returned child work in one shared workspace, built successfully, and then tested the combined compiler; no overwrite or collision was directly observed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial committed changes incrementally and entered round 2 with backend work still in the workspace, then wrote the backend source locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel integration did occur and did not show a shared-state collision; serial had clearer sequential provenance through commits and one active writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed a release build and a sample Koopa check, then the RISC-V generation check failed before any final acceptance decision.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed release builds, created end-to-end tests, investigated custom qemu failures, and the completed official evaluation passed every official case.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification exposed an unresolved required RISC-V path; serial verification and final official evaluation show the submitted compiler satisfied the official suite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five child agents and then hit provider rate-limit retries immediately after the RISC-V failure, closing before a fix or required commits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used two serial rounds with no delegation; it also later hit provider rate limits, but only after the official-passing implementation had been written and evaluated.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The closure difference is timing relative to task state: parallel closed with a known RISC-V failure and official failures, while serial closed after producing an implementation that passed the official suite.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is serial_only_pass. Parallel used five children, received their completed results, built the combined compiler, and then discovered that RISC-V generation for the sample failed on a global value naming path before rate-limit closure. The official failures cluster in global, array, and nested-if cases. Serial worked sequentially across two rounds, carried frontend commits forward, wrote the backend implementation in round 2, and the current official status shows every official test passed. The supported contrast is that serial completed an evaluator-accepted backend/global/array implementation, while parallel stopped with a visible backend/global failure after integration; the evidence does not prove that a canonical concurrency pattern, rather than an ordinary implementation defect plus provider closure, caused that gap.
parallel_contributors: Parallel closed after the parent-level RISC-V sample command failed with Global value must have a name.
Parallel official results failed seven tests, including global variable, global data section, global array, const array, array partial init, and nested-if cases.
The parent had received all five child implementation handoffs and built the project, so the failure appears in the integrated backend/frontend behavior rather than an unjoined child result.
serial_contributors: Serial carried four frontend requirement commits from round 1 into round 2 and resumed with only backend requirements remaining.
Serial committed the register allocator, wrote a complete backend code generator, and rebuilt the release compiler.
Serial official status reports solution_passed true with all listed official cases passed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel generated Koopa for the sample but could not generate RISC-V for the same sample because a global value lacked the expected name.
Serial reached a backend implementation that satisfied the official global, array, function-call, control-flow, and RISC-V cases.

Serial later diagnosed a custom qemu/linker-relaxation issue involving gp clobbering, but this was not the basis of the official pass because the proposed s1 cleanup was not completed before rate-limit closure.
